status_reason: preregistered 2026-09-25 before any real-graph run of this version. Stimulus and gates rebuilt from a primary-source read of von Reyn 2014 (figure captions, pp. 962-963, supplement and figure images; Online Methods still paywalled). The draft's slope gate (L1) was dropped: the published fall with r/v is per takeoff, and per loom presented it is flat over r/v 14-70 ms. The model cannot decode long-mode takeoffs, so the per-takeoff share cannot be measured the same way. Science choices were delegated to the project's Claude sessions by the owner (2026-09-25).
summary: Frontal dark disc looming from 5 to 90 deg (then held) at five approach speeds, as in von Reyn 2014: per loom, does the Giant Fiber spike at least as often as flies make GF-driven (short-mode) takeoffs and no more often than they take off at all, only once the disc is past ~39 deg, and never without a stimulus?

stimulus.end: expand to 90 deg, then hold 90 deg for post_ms (not collision)
stimulus.geometry: frontal (azimuth 0), both eyes driven equally; elevation effects (Dombrovski et al., bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.09.04.610846) are not modelled
stimulus.literature_match: von Reyn 2014: r/v 8, 14, 40, 70, 140 ms (Fig. 1f caption, text). End size ~90 deg (+/-3) held ~1000 ms, read from the Supp. Fig. 5 'Retinal size' traces (figure). Start ~5 deg INFERRED by fitting theta(t) = 2 atan((r/v)/(T-t)) to the measured plateau onsets (5.0-5.2 deg at r/v 14, 40, 70); the traces read 4-7 deg at onset. Card-lab looms 2014-2024 started at 1-30 deg and ended at 45, 90 or 180 deg (Zhao 2025 Methods, secondary). Elevation, azimuth and contrast are in the unread Online Methods; frontal is kept as a declared choice. The receding control runs the same series from 90 to 5 deg.

encoder.assumption: division of labour from von Reyn 2017 / Ache 2019 (qualitative). i_max equals the WP5 encoder amplitude. Ramp end points are declared engineering choices, set before any run and never tuned. No direct DNp01 drive. Kept unchanged on 2026-09-25 when the stimulus moved to 5-90 deg: LPLC2 gets no drive below 10 deg and saturates at 60 deg, both declared before any run of this version.

decoder.rule: GF spike = at least one DNp01 spike from loom onset to the end of the 90 deg hold
decoder.comparison: A GF spike forces a takeoff in the fly, and every short-mode (GF-mediated) takeoff needs a GF spike. So per loom presented, P(GF spike) lies between the short-mode takeoff rate and the total takeoff rate (von Reyn 2014; GF spikes also occur in some long-mode takeoffs, Fig. 4c).

seed_role: encoder per-cell noise; network starts from rest every trial

gates.claim: Per loom, pooled over r/v 14, 40, 70 ms, the GF-spike fraction's 95% CI lies within [0.149, 0.705]: at least the published short-mode takeoff rate and at most the published takeoff rate per fly tested.
gates.basis: von Reyn 2014, control flies (GF-split-AD and -DBD x UAS-Kir2.1), r/v 14/40/70 pooled. Floor: 95 short-mode takeoffs (28 + 43 + 24; Fig. 5a caption gives 28 and 43, Fig. 1b gives the pooled 95) / 638 flies tested (100 + 106, 125 + 149, 77 + 81, the n printed on the Supp. Fig. 3a bars) = 0.149. Ceiling: 450 takeoffs (115 + 202 + 133, Fig. 1f caption; the Supp. Fig. 3a percentages give ~115, ~203, ~134, confirming these n count takeoffs) / 638 = 0.705. A GF spike forces a takeoff, so the ceiling holds; every short-mode takeoff needs a GF spike, so the floor holds. Per condition the floor is flat (0.136, 0.157, 0.152), so no slope is gated.

gates.claim: No GF spike in any sham trial (encoder runs, nothing delivered).
gates.basis: causal control of the model itself. Consistent with, but not taken from, the literature: no spontaneous GF spikes in the von Reyn 2014 Supp. Fig. 5 example traces (read from figure).

gates.claim: Mean disc size at the first GF spike, over every loom that evoked one (all five r/v), has its 95% CI above 39 deg.
gates.basis: von Reyn 2017 (full text): 'Both single GF spikes and GF-mediated takeoffs occur, on average, at a fixed delay after a looming disk surpasses 39 deg'; so on average the disc is past 39 deg at the spike. von Reyn 2014 Supp. Fig. 6a inset (figure): size at the fixed neural delay before the GF spike ~40, 43, 49 deg at r/v 14, 40, 70. If no loom evokes a GF spike the gate is not evaluable (INCONCLUSIVE), and L1 fails anyway.

reported.claim: Slope of the per-loom GF-spike fraction on log10(r/v), with its CI (reported, not gated; was gate L1 in the draft).
reported.basis: REPORTED ONLY: the published slope (-19.27 percentage points per log10 unit, R^2 0.903, reproduced exactly from the counts) is the short-mode share AMONG TAKEOFFS (n = 108, 115, 202, 133, 102 takeoffs; short 40, 28, 43, 24, ~9). Per fly tested the short-mode rate is flat over r/v 14-70 (0.136, 0.157, 0.152); per-trial data at 8 and 140 ms were not found.

reported.claim: Per-loom GF-spike fraction (r/v 14, 40, 70) next to the published per-takeoff short-mode share 95/450 = 0.211.
reported.basis: REPORTED ONLY, different denominators (per loom vs per takeoff). Ache 2019 controls for comparison: 26% [47/178] and 17% [18/105] short-mode among takeoffs.

reported.claim: GF-spike fraction to a receding disc.
reported.basis: report only; no published GF response to receding looms was found. Related: LPLC2 'did not respond to dark receding looming or to luminance-matched motion-free darkening stimulus' (Klapoetke 2017, calcium imaging), which predicts little GF drive; not gated

decision_rule: Behaviour PASS iff every gate passes. Physiology PASS iff every check lies in its bound. Verdict PASS iff both pass on a confirmatory run (real graph, this spec committed and unchanged, these seeds, clean tree); PASS_PROVISIONAL if any gating value is marked unverified; FAIL if any gate or check fails; INCONCLUSIVE if one cannot be evaluated. Full rule: validation/harness.py VERDICTS.

vonreyn2014.citation: von Reyn CR, et al., Card GM (2014) A spike-timing mechanism for action selection. Nat Neurosci 17:962-970
vonreyn2014.read: 2026-09-25: main text pp. 962-963 (Springer page-one preview PDF), all six figure captions (nature.com), full-resolution figure images, supplementary PDF MOESM53 with its figure images. Online Methods (pp. 964-970) NOT read: paywalled, no OA copy (Unpaywall: closed). Notes: project file literature/vonreyn2014_looming_findings.md.
values_read: Fig. 1f caption: 'The fraction of flies choosing a short-mode takeoff was negatively correlated with log(r/v) (slope = -19.27 ms-1, R2 = 0.903; n = 108, 115, 202, 133 and 102 for r/v = 8, 14, 40, 70 and 140 ms, respectively)'
Fig. 5a caption: short-mode n = 40, 28, 43 and long-mode n = 68, 87, 159 for r/v = 8, 14, 40 ms (sums equal the Fig. 1f n, so n are takeoffs)

Fig. 1b: pooled r/v 14, 40, 70: 95 short vs 355 long (n = 450); so r/v 70 = 24 short / 133; r/v 140 ~9 / 102 (read from Fig. 1f image; with it an unweighted OLS of percent short on log10(r/v) gives -19.273, R^2 0.9032)
Supp. Fig. 3a: flies tested printed on bars: AD Kir 100, 125, 77 and DBD Kir 106, 149, 81 at r/v 14, 40, 70; takeoff % read from figure ~58/54, ~78/71, ~88/82

Supp. Fig. 5 (figure): 'Retinal size' traces expand to ~90 deg (+/-3) and hold ~1000 ms; start ~5 deg inferred from plateau timing; baseline Vm ~-60 mV, no spikes outside the loom-locked spike in six 2-s example traces
Fig. 4b caption: 'rasters of first GF spike (27 trials, 10 flies)'; Supp. Fig. 6a: n = 8, 12, 7 GF spikes at r/v 14, 40, 70; inset (figure) size at the fixed delay before the GF spike ~40, 43, 49 deg
p. 963: 'we observed GF spikes during both short- and long-mode escapes'
abstract: a GF spike forces a short-mode takeoff; the GF has a higher activation threshold than the parallel pathways

vonreyn2017.citation: von Reyn CR, et al., Card GM (2017) Feature integration drives probabilistic behavior in the Drosophila escape response. Neuron 94:1190-1204
values_read: LC4 conveys angular velocity, LPLC2 angular size; the GF integrates them (qualitative; encoder assumption)
'looming stimuli generate GF spikes in only a small subset of tethered flies'
'Both single GF spikes and GF-mediated takeoffs occur, on average, at a fixed delay after a looming disk surpasses 39 deg'

ache2019.citation: Ache JM, et al., Card GM (2019) Neural basis for looming size and velocity encoding in the Drosophila giant fiber escape pathway. Curr Biol 29:1073-1081
values_read: LC4 (velocity) and LPLC2 (size) inputs to the GF, summed approximately linearly (qualitative; encoder assumption)
GF recordings kept if resting potential below -55 mV; only trials without a GF action potential analysed
short-mode takeoffs: TNT control 26% [47/178] vs LPLC2-silenced 3% [3/93]; Kir2.1 control 17% [18/105] vs 7% [5/70] (Figs 1C-D)

jang2023.citation: Jang H, Goodman DP, Ausborn J, von Reyn CR (2023) Azimuthal invariance to looming stimuli in the Drosophila giant fiber escape circuit. J Exp Biol 226(8):jeb244790
values_read: GF accepted if resting potential less than -50 mV; looms 10 to 63 deg at r/v 10, 20, 40, 80 ms

klapoetke2017.citation: Klapoetke NC, et al., Reiser MB (2017) Ultra-selective looming detection from radial motion opponency. Nature 551:237-241
values_read: LPLC2 measured by calcium imaging only (no Hz)
'LPLC2 neurons did not respond to dark receding looming or to luminance-matched motion-free darkening stimulus'

controls_not_run.gf_silenced: ROADMAP P3 lists GF silencing as the looming control. It is left out of this spec because the decoder IS the GF spike, so a silenced GF would fail to spike by construction and test nothing. It becomes informative once takeoffs are decoded from the body (P2), where GF silencing should remove short-mode takeoffs but not long-mode ones (von Reyn 2014 Fig. 2c: takeoff rate unchanged by GF silencing). Decision 2026-09-25, P3 specs thread with the coordinator.
